95e5d8c4ba.q: What is Coles and Keys optical and what makes it different from traditional optometry clinics?
95e5d8c4ba.a: Coles and Keys is an independent eyewear optical featuring handcrafted, boutique eyewear by independent designers who don't work for large conglomerates. They carry frames and lens companies that believe people deserve to be treated well and paid fairly for quality work, ensuring both employees and customers receive lasting, carefully crafted products. The founders created a welcoming space where people can come as they are and express themselves through incredible eyewear, rejecting the clinical scenarios typical of traditional optometry.

8fc74eec66.q: Why did Nikki and Nicole decide to leave their positions at established optical clinics to start their own business?
8fc74eec66.a: Nicole felt the business had shifted from being about people to being about numbers and money, causing her to burn out in her early 30s and lose parts of her soul. After visiting a warm, welcoming optical in Toronto that inspired them, she and Nikki began dreaming about opening their own place. The turning point came when Nikki said, 'What if it's not one day, what if it is today?' Nicole decided she wanted to maintain her passion for eyewear, have fun, stay true to herself, and do this as a meaningful career rather than burn out.

c19f24dcea.q: How did the COVID-19 pandemic influence Nikki and Nicole's decision to create a different kind of optical experience?
c19f24dcea.a: During COVID, both worked in clinical optical settings with masks, plexiglass barriers, and 15-minute in-and-out appointments that prevented them from showing personality or being personal with clients. They recognized that people felt vulnerable removing their glasses and wanted to create a space where clients felt welcome, embraced, and safe rather than treated like cattle or feeling clinical. Coming out of the pandemic when people were fragile and still recovering, they committed to ensuring clients would know they belong and are cared for, maintaining warmth even with physical distance.

26efe7e550.q: What does 'wearable art' mean in the independent eyewear industry, and how does designer Blake Kuhara exemplify this concept?
26efe7e550.a: Wearable art is an industry term in the independent eyewear world describing glasses as crafted artistic pieces. Designer Blake Kuhara exemplifies this by creating frames grounded in architectural history; his acetate frames in the mainstay collection are named after architects and their impacts. His design process considers line work, engineering, comfort, and functionality as carefully as an architect designs buildings and public spaces, ensuring that every frame element serves both artistic intention and practical purpose.

70225cc515.q: How do Nikki and Nicole position eyeglasses as a multi-year investment in personal identity and presentation?
70225cc515.a: They frame glasses as your 'next chapter' because most people don't have multiple pairs and will be remembered in these glasses across all photos and social interactions for the next two to five years. Since glasses sit directly on your face and are visible in family photos, friend photos, and all presentations, they represent how you will be remembered and how you present yourself to the world. Investing in frames made with intention, passion, and craftsmanship ensures you project a carefully considered version of yourself outwardly.
